subject.title: Per-account native command prefix for multi-agent slash commands

question: Should Slack multi-account native slash commands be solved with validated account-level `nativeNames` mapping, constrained `nativePrefix` sugar, or documented as unsupported for duplicate native command names?
rationale: Current main has no account-level naming contract, and the two closed implementation PRs show a real design fork; adding either path expands a user-visible Slack config/API surface that repository policy treats as product-sensitive.

options.title: Implement validated nativeNames
options.body: Add one explicit per-account mapping surface with duplicate and Slack-name validation, registration and reverse lookup support, docs, and tests.

options.title: Implement constrained nativePrefix
options.body: Add prefix sugar only with strict lowercase slug validation and no broad dash-stripping fallback, accepting simpler setup but another naming abstraction.

options.title: Document unsupported duplicate names
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document that multiple Slack apps in one workspace must not register identical native command names.

recommendation.title: Implement validated nativeNames
recommendation.body: Add one explicit per-account mapping surface with duplicate and Slack-name validation, registration and reverse lookup support, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant historical commits for Slack native names and shared command registry behavior point to steipete.
